newsitem.title: USA: CIA report said to question Jiang's control.
newsitem.headline: CIA report said to question Jiang's control.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin has failed to consolidate his grip on power, a fact that will keep him focused on domestic rather than global issues, according to a classified U.S. report quoted in Friday's Washington Times.
The newspaper said it had obtained a copy of a CIA report prepared in June and labeled "top secret" which questioned Jiang's hold on power.

The newspaper quoted a U.S. government official familiar with the report as saying that Jiang had shown "remarkable staying power" but the real test of his skills would come at the country's 15th party congress this October.
Jiang is the designated Communist Party leader after the death on Wednesday of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
The CIA report said at least seven rivals were "trying to limit his power" before the meeting.

It said there were signs that Jiang had failed to consolidate his grip on power, despite seven years as the general secretary of the Communist Party, six years as Central Military Commission chairman and three years as president, the Washington Times reported.

"Jiang's inability to consolidate his power means he will remain focused on domestic issues and is unlikely to initiate any steps to improve relations with the U.S. or Taiwan that could spark international criticism," it quoted the report as saying.
No comment was immediately available from the CIA.
